name: Moscow, Third Rome
summary: The doctrine, formulated by the monk Filofei in sixteenth-century Muscovy, holds that Rome fell to heresy, Constantinople to the Turks, and that Moscow is the third and last Rome, the sole remaining seat of true Orthodox Christianity. The God-chosen ruler must guard the Church, keep the inherited Christian order and not seize church property. Scholars stress that the original letters say little beyond this and that its imperial and messianic readings came later.
scope: The sixteenth-century doctrine as stated in Filofei's letters (the translated excerpt, s1) and as the reference works and Poe's scholarship describe it (s2, s3, s4). It excludes later Holy Russia, Slavophile, Soviet and modern nationalist uses, which the same scholarship treats as later appropriations.
